papers.title_in_file: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm with random and subgraph phase operators
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of QAOA for MaxCut in which the phase operator is replaced by random, subgraph, triangle-removed or max-degree-edge-removed variants.

assertions.value: The authors report that, at p = 1, 0.036% of the random custom phase operators, 75.9% of the subgraph custom phase operators, 95.1% of the triangle-removed custom phase operators and 93.9% of the maximal degree edge-removed custom phase operators have a higher approximation ratio than the original QAOA implementation, out of all graphs tested.
quotes: Out of all the graphs tested at p = 1, 0.036% of the random custom phase operators, 75.9% of the subgraph custom phase operators, 95.1% of the triangle-removed custom phase operators,
and 93.9% of the maximal degree edge-removed custom phase operators have a higher approximation ratio than the original QAOA implementation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The percentages count phase operators in the paper's sample, not a general rate.

assertions.value: The authors state that they tested the phase operators for the MaxCut problem on all 11,117 non-isomorphic eight vertex graphs, using the L-BFGS optimizer with 100 random parameter initialization seeds.
quotes: for solving the MaxCut problem on all 11,117 non-isomorphic eight vertex graphs.
The optimizer used was the L-BFGS algorithm with 100 random parameter initialization seeds.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup, Section III, p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that up to 10 non-isomorphic random phase operators were considered per graph, and that there are far more than 10 non-isomorphic phase operators that can be generated in most cases, so the remaining graphs may have better phase operators.
quotes: For each graph, up to 10 non-isomorphic random phase operators were considered.
Furthermore, there are far more than 10 non-isomorphic phase operators that can be generated in most cases, so it is of course possible that the remaining graphs have better phase operators.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limit of its sampling, Section III.A.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Federated Learning with Entanglement Controlled Circuits and Superposition Coding
papers.what_it_is: Proposes entangled slimmable quantum neural networks and an entangled slimmable quantum federated learning scheme with superposition-coded parameter transmission, evaluated by simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that extensive simulations corroborate the effectiveness of eSQFL in terms of global eQSNN prediction accuracy compared to Vanilla QFL.
quotes: extensive simulations corroborate the effectiveness of eSQFL in terms of global eQSNN prediction accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study, in an abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MNIST data is reduced to 4 × 4 by inter-area interpolation and that only four classes are used (0, 1, 2 and 3).
quotes: the dimension of MNIST data is reduced to 4 × 4 by inter-area interpolation, and only four classes are used (i.e., 0, 1, 2 and 3)
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own experimental setup, Section VI.A.

assertions.value: The authors report that as the channel quality increases from 11 dB to 19 dB, the decoding success probability and top-1 accuracy of the eSQFL with all layers increase.
quotes: increases from 11 dB to 19 dB, the decoding success probability and top-1 accuracy of the eSQFL with all layers increase
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in future research, they will apply the model to a plethora of real-life scenarios with various limitations.
quotes: In our future research directions, we will apply it to a plethora of real-life scenarios with various limitations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion states that real-life testing is future work.
assertions.reader_inference: The reported results are simulations on a reduced MNIST task, not hardware runs.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient and quantum-adaptive machine learning with fermion neural networks
papers.version_note: The file name carries the v1 title (A quantum neural network with efficient optimization and ...); the text is the v3 revision dated 17 Sep 2023 of arXiv 2211.05793, titled Efficient and quantum-adaptive machine learning with fermion neural networks. Same paper, revised title.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes fermion neural networks, a fermion model whose physical properties serve as outputs, trained for MNIST and for classifying topological phases and charge orders.

assertions.value: The authors report that a fully-connected FNN reaches 98.13% accuracy on MNIST and a locally-connected FNN reaches 97.36% accuracy.
quotes: With a fully-connected FNN, we reach 98.13% accuracy (Fig. 2)
we still reach a satisfactory 97.36% accuracy with a locally-connected FNN
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for models with moderate disorders the FNNs with LDOS (CC) output achieve 99.83% (99.51%) accuracy in inferring the topological phase.
quotes: Even for models with moderate disorders, the FNNs with LDOS (CC) output achieves 99.83% (99.51%) accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a strongly correlated model the accuracy reaches 99.7%, and note that the FNN confidence is not very high.
quotes: We note that the accuracy reaches 99.7%
However, the FNN confidence is not very high, which is typical for machine learning of metal-insulator transitions
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result and caveat from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the state-of-the-art MNIST accuracy of 99.87% is achieved by ensemble learning with homogeneous vector capsules and convolutional neural networks, and that FNNs have much room for faster convergence and better accuracy.
quotes: The state-of-the-art 99.87% accuracy is achieved by ensemble learning with homogeneous vector capsules and convolutional neural networks
FNNs have much room for faster convergence and better accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' footnote, no evidence given for the room to improve.

papers.title_in_file: Dual-Capability Machine Learning Models for Quantum Hamiltonian Parameter Estimation and Dynamics Prediction
papers.what_it_is: An LSTM-based model that infers time-dependent Hamiltonian parameters from local observables and predicts observable dynamics, tested in simulation, on an NMR quantum computer and on a superconducting device.

assertions.value: The authors state that they developed a machine learning framework that utilizes LSTM to predict quantum dynamics and infer Hamiltonian parameters, and that it can deduce time-dependent Hamiltonian parameters from local observables and predict their evolution from Hamiltonian parameters.
quotes: it can deduce time-dependent Hamiltonian parameters from observed changes in local observables within quantum many-body systems, and it can predict the evolution of these observables based on Hamiltonian parameters.
we have developed a machine learning framework that utilizes LSTM to effectively predict quantum dynamics and infer Hamiltonian parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own description of its model, Abstract and Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors report that the model was trained on noiseless evolutions across systems of different sizes (N = 5, 7, 9, 11) and that in the extrapolation period losses increased, peaking at around 10−2.
quotes: Our models were evaluated by training on noiseless evolutions across systems of different sizes (N = 5, 7, 9, 11).
although losses increased, peaking at around 10−2, they remained relatively low
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the NMR experiment used a desktop NMR quantum computer whose device comprises two qubits, and that for the superconducting device the low MSE(1%) underscores the model's capability to infer detuning.
quotes: the device comprises two qubits, represented by the nuclei 1H and 31P in Dimethylphosphite molecules
The low MSE(1%) underscores the model
assertions.certainty_reason: Experimental result from one study on two-qubit devices.

assertions.value: The authors report that fluctuations in the loss tend to increase over time, leading to a statistical rise in the overall loss.
quotes: the fluctuations in the loss tend to increase over time, leading to a statistical rise in the overall loss
assertions.certainty_reason: Observation from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Machine Learning with Quantum Error Detection
papers.what_it_is: A classical simulation of a 2-qubit parity-classifying variational quantum classifier encoded in the [[4,2,2]] error-detecting code under two noise models.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study a simple parity-classifying Variational Quantum Classifier implemented with the [[4,2,2]] error-detecting stabiliser code in a simulated noisy environment, through classical simulations of a 2-qubit VQC.
quotes: we investigate the performance of a simple, parity-classifying Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) implemented with the [[4,2,2]] error-detecting stabiliser code in a simulated noisy environment
Through classical simulations of a 2-qubit VQC implemented with the [[4,2,2]] code
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own setup, Abstract and Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that the stabiliser code improves the training accuracy at convergence compared to noisy implementations without QEC.
quotes: We demonstrate that the stabiliser code improves the training accuracy at convergence compared to noisy implementations without QEC.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report a threshold Pauli Error Rate of p = 0.003 for the gate noise model and p = 0.004 for the environmental depolarising noise model, for a desired minimum training accuracy of 0.90.
quotes: we arrive at a threshold Pauli Error Rate of p = 0.003 for the gate noise model, and p = 0.004 for the environmental depolarising noise model
for a desired minimum training accuracy of 0.90
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation-derived threshold from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that for QML implementations with QEC codes that require ancilla qubits for logical rotations and cannot fully correct errors propagated between ancilla and physical qubits, the maximum achievable accuracy of the QML model is limited.
quotes: for QML implementations with QEC codes that both require ancilla qubits for logical rotations and cannot fully correct errors propagated between ancilla and physical qubits, the maximum achievable accuracy of the QML model is limited.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion drawn from simulations of one small code and model.

papers.what_it_is: Proposes a scalable QCNN (sQCNN) with multiple filters and a fidelity-based training regularizer (RF-Train), evaluated by simulation on MNIST and FMNIST.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose a new version of QCNN, named scalable quantum convolutional neural network (sQCNN), and a novel training algorithm (RF-Train) that enables sQCNN to diversify the extracted features.
quotes: we propose a new version of QCNN, named scalable quantum convolutional neural network (sQCNN)
This paper proposes a scalable QCNN (sQCNN) architecture and a novel training algorithm (RF-Train) that enables sQCNN to diversify the extracted features.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own proposal, Abstract and Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that sQCNN with high RF-regularizer parameter (λ = 0.5) achieves 16% higher top-1 accuracy than sQCNN which does not utilize RF-Train (λ = 0).
quotes: sQCNN with high RF-regularizer parameter (λ = 0.5) achieves 16% higher top-1 accuracy than sQCNN which does not utilize RF-Train (λ = 0)
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that as the number of qubits increases from 8 to 16, the performance of QCNN drops about 30%.
quotes: As the number of qubits increases from 8 to 16, the performance of QCNN drops about 30%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments use the MNIST and FMNIST datasets, and describe them as simple data with one input channel.
quotes: corroborate the superiority of sQCNN with RF-Train in MNIST and FMNIST datasets, widely used in the literature
simple MNIST and FMNIST data with one input channel
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own statement of the datasets used.
assertions.reader_inference: Results cover only small image tasks.

papers.title_in_file: Robust Quantum Reservoir Computing for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.what_it_is: Applies quantum reservoir computing embeddings to predict molecular activity on MMACD datasets and compares them to classical models, in numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that QRC embeddings appear to improve on the classical model performance for small training data sizes (100 and 200 records), while for larger subsamples of 800 records the classical input features yielded similar performance across an average of 5 runs.
quotes: the QRC embeddings appear to result in an improvement upon the classical model performance for small training data sizes (e.g., 100 and 200 records)
For larger subsamples consisting of 800 records, the classical input features yielded similar performance as the QRC embedded features across an average of 5 runs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that test mean square error is reported for the five smallest datasets in MMACD and averages are reported across five dataset subsamples.
quotes: Test mean square error (smaller is better) is reported for the five smallest datasets in MMACD
In all cases, we report averages across five dataset subsamples
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own evaluation setup, Fig. 2 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QRC performance advantage size is generically comparable to the performance error estimates, and call this the main caveat of their results.
quotes: We note, however, that the QRC performance advantage size is generically comparable to the performance error estimates.
the main caveat of our results and the large uncertainty estimates that result from modeling on small dataset sizes
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own caveat, Section III.A and IV.

papers.title_in_file: Learning Quantum Processes with Memory - Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and appendix passages on universality and training; not the full appendices.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes fully quantum recurrent neural networks built from dissipative quantum neural networks and a quantum training algorithm, evaluated by classical simulation on delay-channel, Hamiltonian-evolution and noise-mitigation tasks.

assertions.value: The authors define a QRNN architecture as universal if it can implement any causal quantum automaton.
quotes: is universal if it can implement any causal quantum automaton
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition stated in the Introduction, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that their QRNNs are universal, i.e. they can be used to simulate general causal quantum automata.
quotes: These are universal, i.e. they can be used to simulate general causal quantum automata.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Discussion without a proof in the main text.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text gives no proof; the appendix was not read for one.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QRNN learns the SWAP channel and generalises well, even for only eight training pairs, while a feed-forward QNN learns worse for every training pair added and does not generalise at all.
quotes: The QRNN learns the SWAP channel
generalises well, even for only eight training pairs.
A feed-forward QNN, by contrast, learns worse for every training pair added and does not generalise at all.
assertions.certainty_reason: Classical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they concentrated on the case of product inputs and outputs, and that they designed benchmarking tasks and classically simulated the training of QRNNs.
quotes: We have concentrated on the case of product in- and outputs
we have designed some benchmarking tasks and classically simulated the training of QRNNs
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own statement of its scope, Discussion.
